robot_upload_rule: D154 (4) / D150 SYNC (1): robot history frames upload PER FRAME AS CAPTURED, for ALL arms, replacing D68's fixed 30-s batches. One `history_batch` record per D2 frame, offered at t0 + the frame's session-local capture time, carrying exactly one frame_ref and one frame's bytes. The record KIND, its fields and the D2 token accounting are unchanged, so the emulator, the coordinator, `cstate` and every arm need no change; `cum_tokens` still carries the session's running total and the 31-token D2 header is still charged once per session, on its first holding (the D101 preload where there is one, otherwise the first frame). ONE INTENDED DIFFERENCE BEYOND PACKAGING, named because it is visible in the counts: under batch-30s a window whose END falls after the run horizon is dropped whole, taking frames captured BEFORE the horizon with it; per-frame keeps every frame captured before the horizon, which is the point of the contract. Earlier cells are labelled upload-30s.
epg_refresh_rule: PROVISIONAL (flash, 2026-11-20), the LITERAL reading of D153. D153 says 'fresh context after N s with no carry-over', which is NOT StudySH-EP's sliding cap: SH-EP capped EP-G at the last 21 frames and its cap bound exactly at its last instant, so SH-EP never exercised a refresh at all and cannot settle this. Implemented here as a FRESH CONTEXT EVERY 21 FRAMES WITH NO CARRY-OVER, N = 21 frames = 10.5 s at the 0.5 s cadence, matching SH-EP's cap. Measured on the committed seed-4 16-device 1200 s 40:40:20 trace (13,193 monitor instants, 189 plays): the literal refresh gives a median 10 frames per request, excludes 1,429 instants at floor 3 (10.83 percent) and costs 46,260,494 prompt tokens per run, against the sliding cap's median 21, 378 exclusions (2.87 percent) and 80,794,968 tokens. The literal reading is implemented because it is what the D-row says and because it halves the token load, which matters at 32 devices. A ruling for the sliding cap changes one function, `_epg_episode`.

outage.nesting_proof: robots == sorted(victim_permutation[:outage_robots_k]); the permutation stream key carries NO k, so for k1 < k2 the k1 victim set is a subset of the k2 victim set and t_start is bit-identical
outage.placement_rule: E1 (scenario switch): the window start is an EXPLICIT t0 supplied by the caller (`outage_t0_s`), identical for every k at a seed, so it carries no k. The victims are the first k of the SAME k-independent permutation the 'centre' rule uses (stream key 'outage-perm|seed|offset|D'), recorded as `victim_permutation`, so victims stay nested in k and equal the centre rule's victims. THE PLACEMENT RULE IS IN THE TRACE-DIRECTORY TOKEN together with t0, or a stale trace would be served. The t0 may be chosen by reading the trace's future questions (legal for scenario design: the policy never sees it); a t0 chosen that way maximises dose by construction and the dose is not an effect size.
outage.rule: D242 item A (PROVISIONAL, placement awaiting a ruling): `outage_robots_k` robots drawn from a dedicated RNG stream keyed on (seed, outage_seed_offset, k, D) lose the uplink TOGETHER for `outage_duration_s` seconds, in ONE window per run whose start is drawn uniformly in [0.25, 0.75] x (run_s - D). INSIDE THE WINDOW NOTHING IS OFFERED. A `history_batch` record's `t` IS its offer time, so its `t` moves to the reconnect instant and `fleet/links.py`'s committed UplinkQueue produces the burst and records `queue_s`; no burst model is written here and links.py is unedited. A `recall_question`'s `t` is the ASK time and the deadline anchor, so it does NOT move: the question gains `t_offer`, read at `fleet/emulator.py::_on_recall_question` and handed to UplinkQueue.send, so the question reaches the cloud only after the reconnect and past its own deadline, and the COMMITTED standing-answer rule (`scorer/score.py::_standing` / `_standing_by_deadline`) leaves the DEVICE's answer standing. No second device-only mechanism exists. `device_answers.jsonl` is untouched, and so are every `opportunity_id` and the monitor and question record order, because only history offer times move.
outage.semantics_rule: D242 item A: the in-window history offers are RE-TIMED to the reconnect instant and the committed UplinkQueue drains them; nothing is lost
